items.entity: cantilever design domain (length L x height H)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and Fig. 1 describe a 2-D cantilever but give no length, height or aspect ratio. Sec. 4 gives only element counts (HNelx = 120, HNey = 60 hexagons). The text does not describe the hexagon size, shape or orientation produced by HoneyMesher, so L:H cannot be worked out. It is 2:1 only if each hexagon fills a cell of equal width and height.
readings: L:H ~ 2.3:1 (regular pointy-top hexagons in staggered rows: 120*sqrt(3)a by 60*1.5a)

items.description: Sec. 4 and Fig. 1 use 120 x 60 hexagonal elements generated by HoneyMesher [9]. The text does not give the hexagon geometry (regular or not, side length, orientation, row staggering, jagged boundaries) or the element formulation. The equivalent structured-grid resolution and element size are therefore not determined.
readings: square Q4 elements matching a regular-hexagon domain aspect ratio (~139 x 60 or 120 x 52)
refined Q4 grid (e.g., 240 x 120) with the filter radius scaled to match

items.entity: concentrated point load at the lower-right corner
items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only 'concentrated point load at the free end', and the Fig. 1 caption places it at the lower-right corner. Its direction and sign are never stated in the text; they are only drawn in Fig. 1.
readings: vertical, +y (upward); gives the same optimal layout as -y

items.entity: concentrated point load at the lower-right corner
items.description: No force value is given in Sec. 2.1 or Sec. 4. The reported compliance C = 2.49342 (Table 2, SIMP, M = 1) depends on it.

items.entity: prescribed volume fraction V_f1 for the single material (M = 1)
items.description: Eq. (1) contains V_fm and Sec. 1 mentions 'prescribed volume fractions', but no number is given anywhere (Sec. 4, Table 2) for the M = 1 run or any other run.

items.entity: field on which the volume constraint is evaluated
items.description: Eq. (1) writes V(x)_m in terms of the design variables x. The stiffness, however, uses the filtered and projected x^phys (Eqs. 2-3, eta = 0.5, beta up to 32). The volumes of x, x-tilde and x^phys differ, so it is unclear which one is constrained.
readings: volume of the projected physical field x^phys
volume of the filtered field x-tilde
volume of the raw design variables x

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid (E1) and void (Emin)
items.description: Only normalized moduli are used (Sec. 3.0.1, Eq. 14, Table 1); no absolute modulus is given. Eq. (14) also gives 0/0 for N_MP = 1 and assigns E = 0 to i = 1. This conflicts with Table 1, which gives phase 1 = 1 and void = 1e-9. For M = 1, the consistent reading is E1 = 1 and Emin = 1e-9.
Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere in Secs. 2-4 or Table 1.

items.entity: 2-D stress state (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The text does not say whether the 2-D cantilever is plane stress or plane strain. Plane strain changes the effective Poisson's ratio to nu/(1-nu) as well as the stiffness scale.
The thickness is not given anywhere. It only scales the compliance value C.

Sec. 3.0.1 introduces p in Eq. (4), but no value is given. Sec. 4 says only that 'all the optimization parameters are kept same'. It is also not stated whether p is constant or raised over the run (continuation).
readings: p = 1 (constant; projection alone drives a 0/1 design)
p raised from 1 to 3 by continuation

items.description: Sec. 4 sets r_fill = 4 without units. Neither the element size nor the hexagon dimensions are given, so the radius in element widths on a structured grid is unclear.
readings: r_min = 4 element widths (r measured in element-centroid spacings)
r_min ~ 2.3 element widths (r = 4 hexagon side lengths, centroid spacing = sqrt(3) x side)

items.description: Eq. (2) uses W_ej but never defines it. Sec. 2.2.1 says only 'classical density-filtering technique'.
readings: linear cone weight W_ej = max(0, r_fill - d_ej)

items.description: Sec. 4 says beta 'starts with 1 and increases up to beta_max = 32'. The update rule, the interval and the number of iterations at each beta are not given.
readings: beta doubled when max |dx| < 0.01 at the current beta (or after an iteration cap)
beta increased gradually (e.g., x1.2 per step) every few iterations up to 32

items.entity: MMA optimizer parameters and objective scaling
items.description: The abstract and Sec. 1 state that MMA is used, but the move limit, asymptote parameters and objective/constraint scaling are not given.
readings: move limit 0.5, standard asymptotes (asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7), unscaled compliance
move limit 0.2, objective normalized by initial compliance

items.entity: stopping criterion / maximum number of iterations
items.description: Sec. 4 reports no convergence tolerance and no iteration limit.
readings: stop when relative compliance change < 1e-4 at beta_max

items.description: The starting values of the design variables x_e are not stated.

items.entity: settings behind the reported SIMP M = 1 result (C = 2.49342)
items.description: Sec. 4 says 'All the optimization parameters are kept same'. For M = 1, the SIMP (Eq. 4) and DMO (Eq. 8) interpolations are identical (E = Emin + (1-Emin)x^p with E1 = 1). Yet Table 2 reports C = 2.49342 for SIMP and 2.6527 for DMO, so the exact configuration behind the SIMP result is uncertain.
readings: settings identical to the DMO/gSF runs (difference comes from implementation details)
some unreported parameter (p, V_f, beta schedule, MMA settings or E1) differed for the SIMP M = 1 run

locator: Sec. 2.1 / Sec. 4, the cantilever beam of Fig. 1, single-material extended SIMP case
